related_resources.reason: Sinusoidal response, superposition, harmonic forcing and resonance.
Direction fields, existence and uniqueness, Euler integration, phase lines and stability.
Parity, shifting, convergence, Gibbs phenomenon and Fourier operations.

authorship.scope: Original foundation-first Fourier and periodic-forcing lecture with non-spoken mathematical companion; earlier manuscripts retained.

prerequisites.reason: Solve a forced damped and undamped oscillator using a harmonic trial function.
Recognize higher harmonics of an otherwise low-frequency periodic signal.
Separate a periodic steady response from an initial-data transient.

recommended.reason: Optional review of sinusoidal motion, period, amplitude and phase.

background: Elementary calculus, sine and cosine, first-order initial-value problems, and basic forced oscillators; no functional analysis or PDE background.
readiness_checks: Solve the exact two-harmonic damped oscillator example.
Verify the linearly growing resonant response in the absence of damping.
State what the harmonic gain can and cannot imply about initial-value trajectories.

description: Derives resonance and damping in periodically forced oscillators, showing how response amplitude depends on driving frequency and why one harmonic can dominate.
